title: bug: qa_approve and qa_reject on an unassigned REVIEW row fall back to the caller as the hand-off seat (task.assignedWorkerId || params.workerId) and set it IDLE with currentTaskId null, so a seat that holds another task loses its own claim pointer while that task still names it as assignee
description:
Filed by the governor from hunt #15's held items (task-928a468d, architect-1dd28c7c, msg-492975dd). Re-verified at tip f76c55f3. It waits in BACKLOG on task-e44fbbf3, which edits the same two tools to fence verdicts on rows parked for a human. The governor promotes it when e44fbbf3 is DONE.

PROBLEM
packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaApprove.ts:118 and qaReject.ts:142 compute `handoffWorkerId = task.assignedWorkerId || params.workerId`. After the verdict, qaApprove.ts:251 and qaReject.ts:384 run `touchWorker(handoffWorkerId, { status: 'IDLE', currentTaskId: null })`.
On an unassigned REVIEW row, the hand-off seat is therefore the caller itself, even when the caller holds another task. The task still says assignedWorkerId = that seat, while the worker record says IDLE with no current task. The board shows the seat idle, and the seat's own bookkeeping (status, currentTaskId) no longer matches the row it owns.

EVIDENCE
Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/A/sideLeads.test.ts, case 2, run at d5431577 in a snapshot; output in sideLeads.vitest.txt. qa-b holds task-2 (REVIEW, assigned to qa-b, currentTaskId task-2, status CODING) and calls qa_approve on unassigned REVIEW task-1. Afterwards task-2 is still assigned to qa-b, but qa-b reads status IDLE and currentTaskId null.

FIX DIRECTION
Idle only the seat that actually held the reviewed row: the captured task.assignedWorkerId. When the row was unassigned, touch no worker, or touch the caller only if its currentTaskId is the reviewed task. Apply this the same way in both tools. Error handling unchanged. Check how e44fbbf3 (landed first) restricts who may give a verdict on an unassigned row, and keep its fence. Sync the qa_approve and qa_reject MCP_SERVER.md sections if they describe the hand-off (ruling msg-71db57ac); if not, the summary says none was owed.

FILES
packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaApprove.ts, qaReject.ts, and one vitest file. Gate: that file plus qaApprove.test.ts and qaReject.test.ts, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout (global rail).
definitionOfDone: A qa_approve or qa_reject on an unassigned REVIEW row leaves a caller that holds another task untouched: its status and currentTaskId still point at its own task. The hunt repro case 2 passes for both tools.
A verdict on an assigned REVIEW row still idles that row's assignee exactly as before (an existing or new regression case).
The behavior is identical in both tools, and the existing qaApprove.test.ts and qaReject.test.ts pass.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: qa_approve and qa_reject set IDLE with currentTaskId null only the seat that held the reviewed row. That is the row's captured assignedWorkerId. On an unassigned REVIEW row it is the caller only when the caller's own worker record has currentTaskId equal to the reviewed task. A seat that holds another task and gives a verdict on an unassigned REVIEW row keeps its status and currentTaskId, so the board and its own bookkeeping still match the row it owns. Everything else about both verdicts is unchanged: the gates and their order, the Review and task writes, chat posts, refusals and return shapes. The workerId-less human path idles the assignee or no one, as before.
acceptanceCriteria: Hunt repro case 2, both tools: qa-b (CODING, currentTaskId task-2) holds REVIEW task-2 (assigned qa-b). After qa-b's qa_approve on unassigned REVIEW task-1, task-1 is DONE; after its qa_reject, task-1 is WORKING. Either way task-2 stays assigned to qa-b and qa-b reads exactly { status: 'CODING', currentTaskId: 'task-2' }.
A caller whose own currentTaskId is the unassigned reviewed row (qa-c, CODING, task-1) still ends { status: 'IDLE', currentTaskId: null } after either verdict.

A workerId-less verdict on task-1 assigned to qa-a (CODING, task-1) unassigns task-1 and idles qa-a. A bystander qa-b holding task-2 is untouched. qaOwnership.test.ts's 'qa_approve releases the assigned QA worker after approval' and 'qa_reject releases the assigned QA worker after rejection' pass unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Touch no worker on an unassigned row (`handoff = task.assignedWorkerId`). Simplest, but it drops the cleanup of a caller whose own pointer is on the reviewed row, which the old fallback did correctly. The (b) tests pin against it, and the architect's mutant run gave 2 failed. (2) A shared util helper: a fourth file for a one-line expression at two call sites. Rejected. (3) A heartbeat-only touch of a caller that is not the hand-off seat: not asked for, and the wrapper's heartbeat sidecar keeps a live seat's lastActivityAt fresh anyway. (4) Reading the caller after updateTask: no benefit under the mutex, and it would move the hunk toward task-77e54ebb's block.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Any seat may give a verdict on an unparked, unassigned REVIEW row, because assertWorkerOwns's unassigned no-op is deliberate (util/enforcement.ts:62-68). Only the parked (needsHumanReview) row is fenced (a5157059). updateTask already releases the prior OWNER on a status change that clears the pointer (taskStore.ts:622-639), but only when the owner's currentTaskId is the task, and it IDLEs only task-bound statuses. The tools' touchWorker is the unconditional IDLE for the captured assignee, and the only write that can reach the caller on an unassigned row. qa_reject's hard-cap park keeps status REVIEW, so updateTask does no prior-owner release there; the captured-assignee touch is what idles that seat and must stay. The prototype was dry-run at d1062cb0: RED 2 failed, GREEN 8 files / 237 passed, full daemon suite 281 files / 7440 passed / 24 skipped, hunt case 2 green. Artifacts are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-fefce964/.
